paragraphs: Renting a home in Ireland costs a lot of money. A new report shows how hard it is for many renters.
The report is from the CSO. This office collects facts about life in Ireland. It looked at money from 2024.
In south Dublin, about one in four renters paid half of their money on rent. It was the same in Fingal, Wicklow and Louth.
In Leitrim, rent was much easier to pay. There, fewer than one in five renters paid more than 40% of their money on rent.
The average rent for a flat with two bedrooms is now €2,204 a month. In Dublin, it is €2,634. This is a new record.
More than 880,000 people rent from private landlords. Most of them are between 25 and 44 years old. Most of them have jobs.
sentZh: 在愛爾蘭租房要花很多錢。
一份新報告顯示，對許多租屋者來說這有多困難。
這份報告來自中央統計局。
這個機構收集關於愛爾蘭生活的資料。
它研究了2024年的金錢數據。
在南都柏林，大約每四個租屋者中就有一人把一半的錢花在房租上。
芬戈、威克洛和勞斯的情況也一樣。
在利特里姆，房租容易負擔得多。
在那裡，把超過40%的錢花在房租上的租屋者不到五分之一。
兩房公寓的平均租金現在是每月2,204歐元。
在都柏林則是2,634歐元。
這是新的紀錄。
超過88萬人向私人房東租房。
他們大多數年齡在25到44歲之間。
他們大多數人都有工作。

paragraphs: A new report shows that many people who rent homes in Ireland are spending a very large part of their income on rent.
The Central Statistics Office (CSO) studied private renters in all 31 local council areas in the country. It looked at how much of their income, after tax, went on rent in 2024.

In south Dublin, 26% of renters spent at least half of their income on rent. In Fingal, Wicklow and Louth, the figure was 25%. In Dublin city, Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown, Galway city, Carlow and Meath, between one in five and one in four renters had the same problem.
The report also looked at people who paid more than 40% of their income. This was 34% in south Dublin and 33% in Fingal, Louth and Wicklow, but only 18% in Leitrim.
Rents are still going up. According to the property website Daft, the average rent for a two-bedroom apartment reached a record €2,204 a month in the second quarter of 2026. In Dublin, it was €2,634.

More than 880,000 people live in private rented homes. The typical renter is 34 years old, and most renters are between 25 and 44. For 73% of them, their main income comes from a job, while 16% depend mainly on social welfare.
The report also looked at landlords. About 62% of them earned less than €60,000 a year in total, and a third were over 65.
sentZh: 一份新報告顯示，愛爾蘭許多租屋者把收入的很大一部分花在房租上。
中央統計局（CSO）研究了全國31個地方議會區的私人租屋者。
它調查了2024年他們的稅後收入中有多少用於房租。
在南都柏林，26%的租屋者至少把一半收入花在房租上。
在芬戈、威克洛和勞斯，這個數字是25%。
在都柏林市、敦萊里-拉斯當、高威市、卡羅和米斯，每五到四名租屋者中就有一人面臨同樣的問題。
報告也研究了把超過40%收入用於房租的人。
這一比例在南都柏林是34%，在芬戈、勞斯和威克洛是33%，但在利特里姆只有18%。
房租仍在上漲。
根據房產網站Daft，2026年第二季兩房公寓的平均月租創下2,204歐元的紀錄。
在都柏林則為2,634歐元。
超過88萬人住在私人出租的住宅裡。
典型的租屋者是34歲，大多數租屋者年齡介於25到44歲。

paragraphs: A quarter of private tenants in several areas around Dublin are spending at least half of their disposable income on rent, according to new figures from the Central Statistics Office (CSO).
The report examined the 'rent burden' faced by private renters across all 31 local authority areas in the State, using data for 2024.

South Dublin had the highest share, with 26% of tenants handing over at least half of their income to landlords. Fingal, Wicklow and Louth were close behind at 25%. In Dublin city, Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown, Galway city, Carlow and Meath, between a fifth and a quarter of renters faced similar costs.

The gap between regions was also clear when the CSO looked at tenants paying more than 40% of their income. That figure reached 34% in south Dublin and 33% in Fingal, Louth and Wicklow, compared with just 18% in Leitrim.

Market rents continue to climb. Figures from the property website Daft show the average monthly rent for a two-bedroom apartment hit a record €2,204 nationally in the second quarter of 2026, rising to €2,634 in Dublin.

The report also offers a profile of renters. More than 880,000 people live in private rented accommodation, and the median age of tenants was 34. Employment was the main source of income for 73% of them, while 16% relied mainly on social welfare.
As for landlords, around 62% had a total gross income below €60,000, and a third were aged over 65.

paragraphs: Fresh data from the Central Statistics Office (CSO) lays bare the strain of renting in Ireland: in several commuter counties around the capital, a quarter of private tenants are surrendering at least half of their disposable income to rent.
The study scrutinised the so-called 'rent burden' borne by private renters in each of the State's 31 local authority areas, drawing on figures for 2024.

South Dublin fared worst, with 26% of tenants devoting half or more of their income to housing costs, while Fingal, Wicklow and Louth trailed only marginally at 25%. Elsewhere, in Dublin city, Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown, Galway city, Carlow and Meath, somewhere between a fifth and a quarter of renters were similarly stretched.

The regional disparity becomes starker still at the 40% threshold. More than a third of tenants in south Dublin exceeded it, as did 33% in Fingal, Louth and Wicklow, yet in Leitrim the proportion was a comparatively modest 18%.

There is little sign of respite. According to the property website Daft, the average monthly rent for a two-bedroom apartment climbed to an unprecedented €2,204 nationwide in the second quarter of 2026, soaring to €2,634 in Dublin.

The report also sketches a portrait of the sector. Upwards of 880,000 people reside in private rented accommodation, with a median age of 34; wages are the principal source of income for 73% of tenants, whereas 16% depend chiefly on social welfare.
Landlords, meanwhile, are far from uniformly wealthy: roughly 62% reported a gross income under €60,000, and a third were over 65.
